summary: Keep the AI configuration as a committed, maintained repository artifact rather than per-developer local state: commit project instructions (CLAUDE.md and/or AGENTS.md, imported or symlinked so one file serves both surfaces), `.claude/rules/`, named agent/subagent definitions and hook configuration to version control; verify each session actually loads them (`/context` → Memory files); and schedule review of these artifacts, since the observed failure mode is set-and-forget — 73.8% of such artifacts are committed once and never modified.

evidence.summary: RAMP across 441 repositories with 97% agreement against independent human annotation: velocity rises 28-38% at all maturity levels, but among agent-first repositories those without committed AI configuration show roughly twice the cognitive-complexity increase (+53% vs +27%) and 1.7x the static-analysis warning increase; authors note the maturity measure is observational and present the findings as hypothesis-generating.

Project CLAUDE.md is the officially designated team-shared scope ('Shared with: Team members via source control'), with /init to bootstrap, /context to confirm loading, .claude/rules/ for modular path-scoped rules, and /doctor to propose trims of a checked-in CLAUDE.md.

AGENTS.md provides the cross-agent committed form of the same artifact under Agentic AI Foundation / Linux Foundation stewardship; Claude Code documents `@AGENTS.md` import or symlink so a single committed file serves both surfaces.

conditions: Repositories where coding agents author a material share of commits
Teams that currently rely on per-developer local instructions, chat-only conventions, or ungoverned agent settings
Projects already tracking complexity or static-analysis warning trends, so the effect is observable
not_applicable_when: Solo throwaway or spike repositories with no shared quality signal

Repositories that already commit AI configuration — there the next step is reviewing it for staleness (see RMD-E04-001 for content and the agent-instruction-maintenance skill for auditing), not adding more
Contexts where committed instructions would leak secrets or environment-specific paths (use CLAUDE.local.md, gitignored)

expected_effect.primary: Agent behavior becomes a reviewed, shared, versioned property of the repository rather than per-developer configuration, which the RAMP data associates with roughly half the post-adoption growth in cognitive complexity and static-analysis warnings at unchanged velocity.

risks: Association is observational; correlated engineering discipline or model capability may explain part of the gap, so the effect must not be presented as causal
Committed configuration decays — 73.8% of artifacts are never modified after their first commit, so a stale file can license outdated conventions
Growing instruction files consume context and reduce adherence (Claude Code targets under 200 lines per file)
Climbing RAMP levels (named agents, multi-agent orchestration) adds operational surface that is not itself evidenced as beneficial
revalidate_when: An independent or causal (non-observational) replication of the RAMP effect
A provider changes where project instructions or agent definitions are expected to live
The repository's own complexity/warning trend fails to respond after adoption
